title: Playing with Art Tatum at the St. Francis
summary: Tatum hired Edwards and others for a gig and played with childlike enthusiasm.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: I also played with Art Tatum for the first time during that period. He was working at a place called the St. Francis down on Eighth Street, and he came to town and he wanted some horns to play with him -- because he always did a single or a trio, you know, a duo... So he hired John Anderson and me and Red Callender and Oscar Bradley. And that was quite an experience, you know. As great as he was, when he played with us, he was like a little kid -- he was so enthused, you know. He just worked and worked and played his heart out, you know. It was really something to see -- and hear.
